newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech floodwaters recede, no rain expected Monday.
newsitem.headline: Czech floodwaters recede, no rain expected Monday.

text.p: Floodwaters fell further in the Czech Republic on Monday, with only a few villages left on alert after torrential rains earlier this month caused the worst floods ever recorded in the country.

The floods, which have devastated parts of central Europe causing billions of dollars of damage, were responsible for 49 deaths in the Czech Republic, most from the initial flooding during the first week of July.
Although the danger has abated on Czech soil, the battle continues to contain swollen rivers in Poland, where 55 people have been killed, and eastern Germany.
Czech weather service (CHMU) forecasters said on Monday that little rain, if any, was expected in the first half of the week.
"In the following days, we don't expect showers or a rise in the level of rivers." said CHMU forecaster Jiri Strachovsky.
The worst-hit areas along the Morava river and its tributaries had shown marked improvement at the weekend, he said.
"The Morava is receding very quickly. At Zidlochovice (on the Svratka) it has fallen about one metre (three feet) over the whole weekend," he said.
Flood warnings have been lifted everywhere except at Zidlochovice.
Two minor watches were in force with high water levels at the town of Straznice on the Morava and Svidnice on the Chrudimka, a tributary to the Labe in the north.
The waters have caused an estimated 50 to 100 billion crowns ($1.45-2.9 billion) in damage to homes, crops, infrastructure and businesses which were forced to close or cut production.
After approving more than 10 billion crowns in relief for the worst flooding on record, including up to five billion crowns in domestic flood bonds, the Czech cabinet is on summer recess.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has gone on holiday to Austria, leaving deputy premier Josef Lux in charge. ($ = 34.65 Czech Crowns)
